name: Edmund Porter
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember the last ladder I climbed without stopping.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Edmund by a small Thursday habit. Edmund checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I can no longer climb the cab ladder. I stood inside its shadow and taught a child the controls from memory.
appearance: Edmund has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for a thin scattering of white hair over the crown. Back on the street, the familiar outfit is an olive canvas jacket with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Edmund steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Edmund has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Edmund knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To teach one child from the quay level.
family: Dev Ferris is Edmund’s second cousin. Edmund gets to change the plan. Dev offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The borrowed bass*, Dev says, “Somebody paid the ticket years ago and never removed it.”
connections: William Marks. A father's dated picture gives a retired crane operator the time of the gull's next meeting.

reactions.situation: A visitor reaches the quay too late to see it
reactions.response: Edmund shows the visitor where the shadow fell and when the next chance comes.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Edmund asks the filmer to lower the phone and gets another familiar face to stand by the person crying.

reactions.response: Edmund asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
